page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with small marginal notes in the left margin. The catchword "bus" stands at the lower right below the last line.

main_text.p: l.2.D. de Reg. jur. & regula jur. in 6. non est sine culpa.sit extra culpam, qui sese negotio alieno immiscer. Respondeo enim, eum alienum negotium non gerere, neque sese immiscere rei ad se non pertinenti, quiid facit, ad quod naturæ lege, & officii necessitate est obstrictus.
Neque obstat 3. Quod passim in legibus agatur de proprii corporis defensione. Neque enim hoc ipsum statuitur ad exclusionem corporis alterius; quod satis fit id aliis legibus esse expressum.

Nec juri civili praxis adversatur, uti notat Berlichius antea allegatus. Et tradit Igneus, in tantum hoc observari, ut si in conspectu multorum, qui rixantes prohibere potuissent, ne[?] se mutuo offenderent, homicidium fuerit commissum,omnes à Principe litteras, quas innocentiæ vocant, obtinere teneantur, qui-

page.notes: The first word of the page is printed with a long s, transcribed as "sit"; the scan is faint there. "immiscer" and "spondeo" are read from the scan as printed. "ne[?]" is a doubtful reading of the word after "rixantes prohibere potuissent," which looks like "ne" but may be a worn letter. The running head ends in a mark that may be a dagger (†) after "VOET"; I have not transcribed it. The word "quibus" is hyphenated across the line end; "bus" is the catchword at the foot.
